chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan Al-Zayyat, who said:

When I had fulfilled my rituals, I passed by Al-Medina, so I asked about Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and was told that he is at Al-Yanba'a. So I went to Yanba'a. He said to me: 'O Hassan, have you walked to over here?' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you, as I disliked going out and not seeing you.' He said (peace be upon him): 'I ate from this vegetable, meaning the garlic, so I wanted to keep away from the Masjid of Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَتَنَحَّى: to keep away / to seclude oneself
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Mosque of the Messenger of God
key_terms.نُسُكِي: my rituals (referring to Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Al-Sadiq stay away from the mosque after eating garlic?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical application of *adab* (etiquette) in communal worship spaces, illustrating the Imam’s sensitivity to sensory distractions like garlic odor. It underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining the sanctity and comfort of the Prophet’s Mosque through personal hygiene and consideration for others.
